speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me understand your condition, how long have these episodes been occurring, and do they happen suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since your dizziness is sudden and position-dependent, could you please describe exactly which head movements trigger the spinning sensation, such as rolling over in bed or looking up? Additionally, have you noticed any new hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or fullness in one of your ears?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The clinical picture of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old with age-related hearing loss is highly specific for BPPV, not migraine. While I understand the suggestion, the symptoms you describe do not fit the typical pattern for migraines.
